title: OneDrive for iOS and Android: annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs
summary: Hold: the briefing treats every encrypting label's user permissions as administrator-defined, but Microsoft also documents permissions assigned by users when applying a label. The roadmap facts and PDF-support control are supported; the claim about when the portal banner appears needs narrowing.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The roadmap says no new administrator action is required.
claims.quote: requires no new admin action.

claims.claim: This roadmap item excludes OneDrive and SharePoint on the web.
claims.quote: This applies to the OneDrive apps for iOS and Android only (not OneDrive or SharePoint on the web).

claims.claim: The OneDrive PDF features page describes general mobile annotation but does not mention sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive iOS Android sensitivity label protected PDF annotation; opened https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/onedrive-pdf-features in full. It documents general annotation steps and contains no sensitivity-label discussion.

claims.claim: Tenant PDF support can be enabled at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Then, if you see a message Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling, select this banner to confirm you want to turn on PDF protection for files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF $true enables tenant PDF support for sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Alternatively, you can turn on PDF support by using PowerShell. Use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF parameter: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF $true

claims.claim: The Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling banner appears only when PDF support is off.
claims.quote: Searched: "Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling" banner only PDF support enabled; read the PDF-support section at learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files. It says "if you see" the banner, not that its visibility depends exclusively on support being off.
claims.fix: Replace the banner-visibility statements in controls[0].note and Governance controls with: 'If the Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling banner is visible, select it to turn on PDF protection for files in SharePoint and OneDrive.'

claims.where: controls[1].ui and api; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No feature-specific tenant UI switch or automation call for disabling protected-PDF annotation in OneDrive mobile is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive mobile protected PDF annotation disable administrator Set-SPOTenant iOS Android; opened learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/onedrive-pdf-features and the Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell/set-spotenant reference; searched its PDF, mobile and annotation text. No such switch found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Which users get which permissions in an encrypting label is decided when an administrator creates or edits the label's access control settings.
claims.quote: Assign permissions now, so that you determine exactly which users get which permissions to content with that label. Let users assign permissions when they apply the label to content.
claims.fix: Replace the permissions-configuration statements with: 'For labels configured with Assign permissions now, administrators define users and permissions in the label's Access control settings in the Microsoft Purview portal. Labels can instead let users assign permissions when they apply the label.' Remove the Before rollout checklist step about reviewing label permissions, which has no controls-table row.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Enabling tenant PDF support can increase the number of files labelled by existing auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: The tenant auto-labeling throughput ceiling is 500,000 files per day.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies. This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no price or licence specific to protected-PDF annotation in OneDrive mobile.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive mobile sensitivity label PDF annotation licensing price; opened learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/onedrive-pdf-features and the Microsoft Purview service description's sensitivity-labeling section. General annotation and protection licensing are stated, but no mobile-annotation SKU or price.

claims.claim: The OneDrive PDF features page names no labelled-PDF-specific licence or feature meter.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive mobile sensitivity label PDF annotation licensing price; read https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/onedrive-pdf-features in full. Its freemium/premium tables name no labelled-PDF licence or annotation meter.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe how annotations are stored on encrypted PDFs in OneDrive mobile.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive sensitivity label encrypted PDF annotation mobile minimum app version storage annotations prerequisite; read learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/onedrive-pdf-features and the Purview PDF-support sections. General save steps are documented, but encrypted annotation storage is not.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not publish a minimum OneDrive iOS or Android app version for this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive sensitivity label encrypted PDF annotation mobile minimum app version storage annotations prerequisite; opened OneDrive PDF features and Purview PDF-support documentation. Search returned Office-app and desktop-sync versions, not a mobile OneDrive version for this feature.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive support uploaded labelled PDFs with or without encryption when sensitivity labels are enabled and PDF support is added.
claims.quote: When you've enabled SharePoint and OneDrive for sensitivity labels and added PDF support. Then, PDFs are supported when you upload a labeled PDF document with or without encryption applied

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document whether tenant PDF support is a prerequisite for mobile annotation.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive sensitivity label encrypted PDF annotation mobile prerequisite EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF; read Purview SharePoint/OneDrive PDF-support documentation and the Set-SPOTenant parameter reference. Listed scenarios do not establish a prerequisite for mobile annotation.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review label access-control permissions, but the controls table has no row for that control.
claims.quote: Review which sensitivity labels apply encryption and which users hold edit rights in each, using the label's access control settings ... Table rows: tenant PDF support; switch for mobile annotation.
claims.fix: The Before rollout checklist step about reviewing label Access control permissions has no corresponding controls-table row. Remove that checklist step to resolve the mismatch without adding an unverified row.
